headline: Hackers cook French supermarket fridges to 50°C, Dragon hauls the ISS its last new solar arrays this morning, Battlefield 6 lands on Game Pass, and Mercedes plots Russell's next engine penalty as Antonelli eyes Austin.

upcoming.what: SpaceX CRS-35 cargo Dragon launches to the ISS, 11:33 Irish time; Battlefield 6 joins Game Pass with Season 5
Castlevania: Belmont's Curse launches on PS5, Xbox and PC
GTWC Europe Endurance finale, 3 Hours of Portimão, 17:00–20:00 Irish time; UFC Edmonton: Buckley vs Malott (main card small hours of Sunday, Irish time)
WEC 6 Hours of Barcelona, 11:00 Irish time, penultimate round
F1 United States GP, Austin; Antonelli's first shot at the title (Irish clocks go back on the 25th)
Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4 releases (pre-order campaign early access from 16 Oct)
UFC 333: Volkanovski vs Evloev, Abu Dhabi

items.headline: Hackers hijack refrigeration at ~300 French supermarkets
items.summary: Overnight on 11–12 October, attackers forced fridge defrost cycles to a 50°C setpoint at Intermarché, U and other stores, mostly via remotely supervised Danfoss controllers; Paris cybercrime prosecutors are investigating. It's a nasty example of exposed industrial controls, and no one has been named as responsible yet.

items.headline: Networking: IonQ to buy segmentation firm Elisity for up to $1.3bn
items.summary: The quantum company is buying the network-segmentation and identity-based access specialist in an all-stock deal, with up to $150m tied to performance.

items.headline: Amazon reportedly in talks to buy Decart for ~$7bn
items.summary: The WSJ reports Amazon is negotiating for Decart, whose software helps AI workloads run across different chip types. Nothing is signed yet.

items.headline: Today: CRS-35 Dragon carries the ISS's final new solar arrays
items.summary: Falcon 9 is due to lift off from Cape Canaveral at 11:33 Irish time with the last pair of roll-out solar arrays, plus the failed Canadarm2 joint's return kit and experiments on artificial retinas and 3D heart tissue. Docking is planned for Thursday.

items.headline: A small star caught slowly eating a brown dwarf
items.summary: MIT astronomers found a star about 300 light-years away siphoning material off a close brown dwarf companion, a rare look at that kind of system.

items.headline: An injectable device that controls nerves without wires or batteries
items.summary: Researchers built a tiny implant that can be injected rather than surgically placed and modulates nerve activity, which could open a new route to treating chronic pain.

sections.title: Gaming
sections.summary: Release week. Nothing new on the watchlist (Witcher 4, Cyberpunk 2, Witcher 3, Borderlands).

items.headline: Battlefield 6 hits Game Pass today alongside Season 5
items.summary: It joins Ultimate and PC Game Pass the same day Season 5 lands, which brings a Las Vegas setting, new maps and weapons, a Halloween event and a server browser. That's well timed before Modern Warfare 4 on the 23rd.

items.headline: Packed week: Boltgun 2 tomorrow, Castlevania on Thursday
items.summary: Planet Zoo 2 and Valor Mortis are out today, Warhammer 40,000: Boltgun 2 and Jackbox 12 follow on Wednesday, and Castlevania: Belmont's Curse arrives Thursday.

sections.title: BJJ & Grappling
sections.summary: No major events this week; a big week for the business side instead.

items.headline: Windows signs the Ruotolo twins
items.summary: Microsoft's Windows brand has sponsored Kade and Tye Ruotolo in what could be one of jiu-jitsu's biggest sponsorship deals. Terms weren't disclosed, so the rumoured seven-figure value is unconfirmed.

items.headline: FloGrappling boss says UFC BJJ is losing money
items.summary: Flo GM Ben Kovacs argued that the UFC's grappling series doesn't add up financially. That's a rival's view, but it adds to the debate about whether pro grappling pays.

items.headline: Fight week: Buckley vs Malott, Blanchfield vs Jasudavicius
items.summary: Saturday's Rogers Place card has Joaquin Buckley against hometown-region favourite Mike Malott at welterweight, with the rebooked Erin Blanchfield vs Jasmine Jasudavicius flyweight bout as co-main.

items.headline: UK: Pimblett's 2026 return looks unlikely
items.summary: Paddy Pimblett gave a frank update on his comeback that suggests he won't fight again this year, even as talk of Topuria or McGregor bouts continues.

items.headline: Tsarukyan to face Neiman Gracie at RAF Abu Dhabi
items.summary: The UFC lightweight contender has been booked against Neiman Gracie on the Real American Freestyle card in Abu Dhabi.

items.headline: Mercedes weigh another Russell engine penalty, ideally in Vegas
items.summary: After Russell went from the back to ninth in Singapore, Mercedes would prefer to take any further power-unit penalty at Las Vegas, where overtaking is easier. They also confirmed Antonelli's upgraded W17 was the quicker spec.

items.headline: Qatar and Abu Dhabi finale still undecided
items.summary: F1 still hasn't ruled on the security-hit Gulf rounds. An 'oven-ready' Imola is on standby for 6 December, and about $180m in fees and freight is at stake.

items.headline: WEC heads to Barcelona with Toyota in control
items.summary: The #8 Toyota leads the Hypercar standings by 10 points from the sister #7, with BMW 23 points behind in the manufacturers' title, ahead of Sunday's first-ever WEC race at Catalunya. Alex Lynn returns at Cadillac.
